items.title: OmniAct: One Policy, One Million Embodiments
items.summary: OmniAct proposes a single policy that transfers task knowledge across diverse robot embodiments while adapting to each robot's unique capabilities.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because it enables scalable, adaptable robot control across varied hardware.

items.title: DiaCap: Jointly Learning Who Speaks When for Audiovisual Dialogue Captioning
items.summary: DiaCap is an audiovisual LLM that jointly generates transcripts, timestamps, and speaker visual descriptions for video dialogues.
items.whyItMatters: It streamlines captioning and diarization, improving accessibility and content analysis for tech developers.

items.title: BioLoom: Scaling Biomedical Vision-Language Models by Learning from the Structure of Scientific Articles
items.summary: BioLoom proposes using the structure of scientific articles to enhance biomedical vision-language models through richer supervision.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a novel way to improve medical AI accuracy without needing more data.

items.title: CoT-Proxy: Cross-Format Transfer for Distilling Long-Horizon Policies
items.summary: The paper proposes CoT-Proxy, a method to transfer chain-of-thought reasoning from closed AI models to new agents via fine-tuning on teacher trajectories.
items.whyItMatters: It enables cheaper, high-quality policy distillation for long-horizon tasks without needing full access to proprietary model internals.

items.title: iWAM: Efficient Action Prediction from World Models without Explicit Future Prediction
items.summary: iWAM proposes efficient proxies to predict actions from world models without costly future scene generation.
items.whyItMatters: It could speed up real‑time AI control while maintaining policy quality.

items.title: BriConstrain: Geometrically Constrained Decoding for Autoregressive Brick Assembly Generation
items.summary: BriConstrain limits a language model’s token choices during decoding to ensure LEGO assemblies are physically valid, avoiding collisions and unattached parts.
items.whyItMatters: It improves reliability of AI-generated designs, saving time and resources for makers and designers.

items.title: A Bias in Disguise: Tiny Gradient Edits Stop a Small Language Model's Thinking Loops and Complement a Frontier Model's Weight Edit
items.summary: Tiny gradient edits dramatically improve a small language model’s reasoning, while large weight edits boost a frontier model’s math accuracy.
items.whyItMatters: Shows how modest tweaks can unlock powerful reasoning in both small and large AI systems.

items.title: Exploratory Midtraining for Robot Policies
items.summary: The paper explores using midtraining to expand robot policy coverage of low-level behaviors for better autonomous learning.
items.whyItMatters: It could enable robots to learn more robustly from limited human data.

items.title: SAG-Mem-1.0 Technical Report
items.summary: SAG‑Mem 1.0 introduces a new method for long‑term conversational memory that retrieves complementary facts across sessions without relying on derived representations.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because it reduces memory construction overhead and preserves source details for more accurate dialogue systems.

items.title: MetaFORGE: A Meta-Learning Framework for Harness Optimization in Automated Code Generation for Parallel Computing
items.summary: MetaFORGE uses meta‑learning to iteratively refine natural‑language prompts, improving correctness and performance of LLM‑generated MPI C code.
items.whyItMatters: It boosts reliability and speed of AI‑generated parallel programs, critical for high‑performance computing tasks.

items.title: Draft Calibration for Speculative Decoding: Accelerating LLM Serving by Matching Draft and Target Distributions
items.summary: Speculative decoding speeds LLM inference by using a lightweight draft model to propose tokens, then verifying them with the target model in parallel.
items.whyItMatters: Improved inference efficiency can reduce latency and cost for deploying large language models.

items.title: Temporal Conditioning for Human Behavioral Cloning in Chess
items.summary: The paper adds a time-aware transformer to chess behavioral cloning, incorporating clock time into move predictions.
items.whyItMatters: It improves model realism by reflecting how time pressure affects human play decisions.

items.title: Reinforcement Learning Can Be Recovered From Its Own Rollouts
items.summary: Broadly speaking, reinforcement learning (RL) post-training converts compute into model capabilities by training on model-generated data. Typically, the rollouts are discarded after each update, and the knowledge acquired during RL resides in the model weights. items.title: GREMLIN: Generating Random Environments for Meta-Learning with Interacting Networks
items.summary: Can randomly parameterized neural environments supply useful experience for learning a reinforcement learning algorithm? We investigate this question using DiscoRL's rule-discovery framework, replacing human-designed training games with sixteen selected neural environments. Each game combines bounded vector dynamics with a random strategy-based reward and an independent outcome reward. After…

items.title: Delegent: A Multi-Agent Harness That Reduces Cost without Sacrificing Performance
items.summary: Agents built on frontier language models are expensive. At every step, the frontier model re-reads its entire context and executes every subtask regardless of its difficulty. This paper explores the simple thesis that much of this cost can be removed by delegating easy subtasks to a small language model, or SLM, that runs on hardware one already owns. To test it, we build Delegent, a simple and…

items.title: EventDiffusion: Learning Native Event Stream Distribution from Videos
items.summary: Event cameras capture asynchronous brightness changes at high temporal resolution, but scarce recordings constrain data-driven research. Sparse RGB observations cannot uniquely determine intervening events since identical frames may correspond to streams with different activity, polarities, and timing. Existing simulators largely rely on prescribed sensor dynamics and estimated brightness…

items.title: AIChipBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Automated AI Accelerator Design
items.summary: A language-model decoder carries state between decoding steps, and in hardware a wrong state update can leave the current token correct and corrupt the output several tokens later, so a design can pass output tests and still be wrong. AIChipBench asks what LLM coding agents need to build such hardware correctly. Agents implement quantized Qwen3.5, Gemma 3, Gemma 4, and Llama 3.2 decoders in…

items.title: The Radar-based Activities of Daily Living (R-ADL) Dataset
items.summary: Monitoring Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) supports safety and well-being for people living at home, especially older adults, and radar sensing is gaining increasing attention in the field of activity recognition for its ability to ensure privacy in the home while also surpassing technical limitations of other sensing modalities. items.title: Uncertainty-Aware Candidate Generation for Entity Linking in Cyber Threat Intelligence
items.summary: Entity Resolution (ER) pipelines often collapse ambiguity into early hard decisions: upstream Named Entity Recognition (NER) selects a single span and type, and downstream Entity Linking (EL) treats that choice as ground truth. items.title: Shifter Quantization: Compact Representations for Native Integer Computation
items.summary: Groupwise quantization is used in LLM quantization to improve accuracy at low bit widths, but grouping weights keeps standard integer MMA from spanning the full dot product for efficient GPU inference.
